label: Curfew Full Lock
info:
Upgrades the flap's own built-in curfew from a one-way lock (exit blocked, entry still allowed) to a full both-ways lock, by following whatever curfew schedule is configured in the app itself - but only once every cat's chip has been seen inside, so a straggler is never locked out of her own home.

## Why
The app's curfew feature only ever blocks exit during the curfew window - cats can still let themselves back in. That's fine for keeping a cat in overnight, but it also means a curfew that's meant to keep a cat safely indoors doesn't stop it wandering back out again a minute later.

Blindly upgrading every curfew to a full lock is worse, though: if a slower cat is still outside when curfew engages, a full lock shuts her out entirely. So this flow tracks each pet's chip via 'Pet Locations' and only escalates once nobody is reported outside.

## How it works
1. 'Device Status' polls the SurePetcare API every 60s (the API's rate limit) for each device's live lock state and configured curfew schedule
2. 'Pet Locations' polls each pet's chip position in parallel and 'Track Pet Locations' keeps a running `anyPetOutside` flag in flow context - true/false once we've seen every chip at least once, otherwise unknown
3. 'Escalate Curfew Lock' inspects `payload.lockingMode`:
   - `-1` (curfew currently engaged) -> only escalates to `{ lockState: 3 }` (locked both ways) if `anyPetOutside` is explicitly `false`; if a cat is out, or we simply don't know yet, it leaves the flap on the app's own one-way lock so she can still get in
   - `-2` (curfew currently released) -> always sends `{ lockState: 0 }` (unlocked), regardless of pet locations
   - anything else -> no action
4. 'Apply Lock State' (a surepetcare-control node) carries out the change

Because this re-asserts the desired state on every poll rather than firing once at a fixed time, a cat coming inside partway through curfew (or a manual unlock, or a dropped request) is picked up within 60s instead of waiting for the next scheduled event.

## Setup
1. Configure the surepetcare-config node with your credentials
2. In the SurePetcare app (or via the API), set up the curfew schedule you want on the flap itself - this flow follows whatever times are configured there, nothing is hardcoded
3. Deploy - polling starts automatically

## Notes
- Errors (network issues, auth failures) are caught and shown in the 'Error' debug tab rather than crashing the flow
- This is a poll-driven escalation, not a replacement for the app's curfew - the app still owns the schedule, this flow just makes the lock it applies stricter when it's safe to
- Still a polling check, not a hardware interlock: a cat squeezing out in the seconds between her chip being seen and the next poll isn't caught. Keep the poll interval at the API minimum (60s) rather than stretching it further
